name: Steel rain funnel
description: A wide galvanised steel funnel for gathering rainwater into a container set beneath it.
notes: 0.5 m across the rim and 0.43 m tall, standing on its spout, a rolled rim, a hanging tab and a coarse strainer in the throat. The funnel is a thin hollow cone, so its bounding box is mostly air. Setting it up outside to catch rain has no field in this draft. The size is a placeholder.

name: Rain catcher kit
description: A tarpaulin rolled up with a bundle of poles and cord, ready to be rigged into a sheet that runs rain into a container.
notes: A blue tarp rolled to 0.9 m by 0.13 m with grommets along its edge, two cord ties, a spare hank of cord on top and four 1.2 m bark poles lashed alongside. The poles stretch the bounding box. Modelled packed, as a player carries it; the rigged state would need item states. The size is a placeholder.

name: Triple-beam balance
description: A mechanical balance with a steel pan and three beams carrying sliding weights, for weighing small samples precisely.
notes: 0.36 m long: a dark cast base, a 140 mm pan on the left, three stainless beams with brass riders, a scale of ticks, a pointer and a zero mark at the right. weighing is a new quality name for measuring out chemistry and cooking ingredients.

name: Pocket barometer
description: A small plastic dial that reads air pressure, so falling weather can be seen coming.
notes: A 64 mm dark plastic case 14 mm deep with a hanging lug, a white dial with ticks, a red needle and blue and yellow marks for rain and fair. The clear cover is left off so the dial shows. Reading the weather waits on the refactor.

name: Sealed hazard canister
description: A heavy steel canister with a bolted lid and a hazard band. Through its narrow sight glass something green shifts as you turn it.
notes: 60 mm across and 100 mm tall: stainless body, eight bolts on a domed lid, a hi-vis band with black chevrons and a teal sight glass; the tiles show the glass opaque. It is heavy for its size, as a thick-walled container would be. Opening it and what comes out wait on the refactor.

name: Ammonia plant pipework
description: A skid of thick-walled pipe runs, two electric compressors and a control cabinet, built to feed gas to an ammonia reactor and power its smaller electrics.
notes: 3 m by 0.9 m and 1.1 m tall: a yellow skid with pipe posts, three flanged steel pipe runs with two gauges, two blue compressors on charcoal motors with risers to the pipes, a white control cabinet with a green screen and a red switch, and cables running to the compressors. The pipes end in open flanges at +x to meet the reactor's inlet and outlet. An open frame of pipes leaves its box mostly air. It is one half of a placed machine with the reactor; whether it gets its own workstation entry or only counts as the reactor's required neighbour waits on the refactor. The size is a placeholder. The iso tile renders dark at this size; the front and side tiles read.

name: Ammonia reactor
description: A salvaged electric pressure vessel rigged to make ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen. Crude, slow and hungry for power.
notes: 2.9 m tall: a 0.7 m steel vessel with domed heads on four legs over a yellow skid, four aluminium heating jacket bands, a red relief valve, a gauge and a thermowell on top, flanged inlet and outlet at +x facing the pipework, a hazard plate, and a white power cabinet with conduit to the jacket. The round vessel, legs and cabinet leave much of the 1.3 m square box empty. ammonia_synthesis is a new quality name for recipes that make ammonia. It needs the pipework beside it and electric power, which wait on the refactor. The size is a placeholder; the iso tile renders dark at this size.

name: Field chemistry analysis kit
description: A hard case of basic lab instruments for checking what a chemical really is: a balance, a spectrophotometer, a melting point block, a pH meter, cuvettes and chromatography paper.
notes: An aluminium case 0.44 m by 0.32 m and 0.14 m deep, modelled open with its foam-lined lid up behind, the instruments in black foam: a white digital balance, a grey spectrophotometer with screen and keys, a white melting point block with a thermometer, a grey pH meter and probe, a rack of six frosted cuvettes and a stack of paper. The raised lid makes the box mostly air; the closed case is about 20 L. analysis is a new quality name.
